fullPassage:
What does it mean to be brave? There is no single definition, but everyone is brave in their own way. Here are three young people sharing their bravest moments in life.

Jason: One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back. The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong. I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor. I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived. I was scared, but I remembered learning CPR at school. I started to push down on his chest, hoping that I was doing it right. A few minutes later, the paramedics rushed in and took over the situation. Luckily, the clerk regained consciousness. After putting the clerk in the ambulance, the paramedics said "Thank you for being brave. You did a wonderful job." It felt great to help save someone's life!

Olivia: I dreamed of being an Olympic track and field athlete. My room was full of medals and awards from races I had competed in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end. I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. At first, I didn't think much of the injury. I thought I would get better soon. But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful. The doctors said my knee injury would prevent me from running again. Every night, I had flashbacks of my injury. I could not watch sports anymore because it was just too painful. So I shut out everything related to sports from my life. Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major called sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and prevention of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears. So I made up my mind and applied to this major. Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field.

Yuna: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I would get scared. I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough courage. Last year, however, was my final chance before graduating from high school. When I saw the poster on the class board, my mind began to fill with thoughts of the school speech contest. I heard a voice growing louder in my head, saying "Go for it!" I decided to sign up for the contest. To make a long story short, I did it. I delivered my speech to the entire school. How did I do? Honestly, I don't remember much from the contest because I was so nervous. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.

questions.passage:
One evening, I went to a convenience store to buy some snacks. No one was at the counter, so I thought the clerk was working in the back.

(A) I immediately called 911 and explained the situation. The operator asked me to perform CPR on the clerk until the paramedics arrived.

(B) The telephone started ringing, but no one came to answer it. I felt something was wrong.

(C) I looked over the counter and saw the clerk lying on the floor.
questions.stem: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전화 울림 → 이상함 느낌 → 카운터 너머 확인 → 911 신고.
det.analysis:
✅ (B)-(C)-(A): (B) 전화 울리지만 아무도 안 받음 → (C) 카운터 너머 점원 발견 → (A) 911 신고
❌ (A)-(B)-(C): 발견 전에 신고 불가
❌ (A)-(C)-(B): 시간순 뒤바뀜
❌ (C)-(A)-(B): 이상함 느낌 없이 바로 발견은 부자연스러움
det.tip: 시간 순서: 전화 울림(B) → 이상함 느끼고 살펴봄(C) → 911 신고(A). 사건의 논리적 흐름.

det.korean: 말할 기회마다 겁남 → 이 두려움이 무대 뒤에 머물게 함 → 그래서 대회 불참.
det.analysis:
✅ (B)-(C)-(A): (B) But 전환+겁남 → (C) This fear=앞의 두려움 → (A) That's why 결과
❌ (A)-(B)-(C): That's why는 원인 뒤에 와야 함
❌ (A)-(C)-(B): 결과가 원인보다 먼저
❌ (C)-(B)-(A): This fear의 지칭 대상(B) 필요
det.tip: But(전환) → This fear(지시어) → That's why(결과). 접속사와 지시어 추적이 핵심.

❌ (C)-(B)-(A): shut out 후에 Then이 와야 함
det.tip: 시간 흐름: 부상 → 고통/차단(B) → 2년 경과(C) → 전환점 발견(A). Then은 시간 경과 후.

det.analysis:

❌ ②: 이미 마음이 채워지기 시작한 후에 용기 부족은 부자연스러움

questions.stem:

I / was / scared / but / I / remembered / learning / CPR / at school
ch: I was scared but I learning remembered CPR at school
I was scared but I remembered learning CPR at school
I was but scared I remembered learning CPR at school
I was scared but remembered I learning CPR at school

det.analysis:
✅ ② I was scared but I remembered learning CPR at school: 원문 일치
❌ ① learning과 remembered 위치 오류
❌ ③ but과 scared 위치 오류
❌ ④ remembered와 I 위치 오류
det.tip: remember + 동명사(-ing): 과거에 ~한 것을 기억하다. remember learning = 배운 것을 기억하다.

This / was / my chance / to stop / running away / from / my problems / and fears
ch: This was to stop my chance running away from my problems and fears
This my chance was to stop running away from my problems and fears
This was my chance to stop running away from my problems and fears
This was my chance running away to stop from my problems and fears

det.korean: 이것이 내 문제와 두려움으로부터 도망치는 것을 멈출 기회였다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: This was my chance + to stop running away from my problems and fears
❌ ①: my chance와 to stop 위치 오류
❌ ②: was와 my chance 위치 오류
❌ ④: running away와 to stop 위치 오류
det.tip: to stop running away from ~: to부정사(목적) + 동명사(stop의 목적어) + 전치사구.

my Olympic dreams / came / to / a sudden end / during / the national / 100-meter / championship race
ch: during the national 100-meter championship race my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end
my Olympic dreams to a sudden end came during the national 100-meter championship race
my Olympic dreams came during the national 100-meter championship race to a sudden end
my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end during the national 100-meter championship race

det.korean: 전국 100미터 선수권 대회에서 나의 올림픽 꿈은 갑작스럽게 끝났다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④: S(my Olympic dreams) + V(came) + 보어(to a sudden end) + 부사구(during ~)

questions.passage: I looked over the counter and saw the clerk ①<u>lying</u> on the floor. I immediately called 911 and ②<u>explained</u> the situation. The operator asked me ③<u>performing</u> CPR on the clerk until the paramedics ④<u>arrived</u>.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: ③ performing → to perform: ask + 목적어 + to부정사 구문.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ performing → to perform: ask + O + to부정사
❌ ① lying: 지각동사 saw + O + 현재분사, 올바름
❌ ② explained: called and explained 병렬, 올바름
❌ ④ arrived: until절의 과거시제, 올바름
det.tip: ask + 목적어 + to부정사: asked me to perform. ask는 동명사를 목적격 보어로 취하지 않는다.

questions.passage: Two years passed and I was still trying to get used to my ordinary high school life without sports. Then one day, I came across an interesting university major ①<u>calling</u> sports medicine. It deals with the treatment and ②<u>prevention</u> of sports injuries. A light bulb went on in my head. This was my chance to stop ③<u>running</u> away from my ④<u>problems</u> and fears.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?

det.korean: ① calling → called: 전공이 '불리는' 것이므로 과거분사(수동).
det.analysis:
✅ ① calling → called: major called sports medicine (수동 — 전공이 불리는 것)
❌ ② prevention: 명사, treatment and prevention 병렬, 올바름
❌ ③ running: stop + 동명사(~하는 것을 멈추다), 올바름
❌ ④ problems: 명사 복수형, 올바름
det.tip: called(과거분사, 수동) vs calling(현재분사, 능동). 전공이 스스로 부르는 것이 아니라 불리는 것.

questions.passage: Ever since I was young, I have admired great public speakers. I hoped to inspire and move audiences like them someday. But every time I had a chance to speak in front of people, I __________ get scared.

det.korean: 과거의 반복적 행동: 사람들 앞에서 말할 기회가 올 때마다 겁이 나곤 했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ would: 과거의 반복적 습관/행동 — every time과 함께 사용
❌ ① used to: 과거 습관이지만 every time과의 조합은 would가 더 적절
❌ ② was used to: ~에 익숙했다, 뒤에 동명사 필요
❌ ③ am used to: 현재 시제, 과거 맥락에 부적절
det.tip: would + 동사원형: 과거의 반복적 행동. every time/whenever와 함께 자주 사용.

questions.passage: My room was full of medals and awards from races I had __________ in. During the national 100-meter championship race, however, my Olympic dreams came to a sudden end.

det.korean: 과거완료: 내가 참가했던(had competed) 경주에서 받은 메달과 상.
det.analysis:
✅ ② competed: had + 과거분사(과거완료). 경주 참가가 메달 획득보다 먼저
❌ ① compete: 동사원형, had 뒤에 부적절
❌ ③ competing: 현재분사, had 뒤에 부적절
❌ ④ competition: 명사, had 뒤에 부적절
det.tip: had + p.p.(과거완료): 대과거. 경주 참가(대과거) → 메달 획득(과거).

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 문제와 두려움으로부터 도망치는(running away) 것을 멈출 기회.
det.analysis:
✅ ① running away: 원문 일치 — stop running away from
❌ ② looking away: 시선을 돌리다, 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ walking away: 걸어서 떠나다, 강도 약함
❌ ④ turning away: 외면하다, 유사하지만 원문 불일치
det.tip: run away from(~로부터 도망치다) — 문제를 직면하지 않고 회피하는 비유적 표현.

questions.passage: I didn't want to make a fool of myself. This fear kept me behind the stage rather than on it. That's why I never entered the annual speech contest at my school. I really wanted to, but I just didn't have enough __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정말 하고 싶었지만 용기(courage)가 충분하지 않았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ courage: 원문 일치 — 두려움(fear)의 반대 개념으로 용기가 부족
❌ ① talent: 재능, 문맥 부적절 (원하는 마음은 있었음)
❌ ② time: 시간, 문맥 부적절
❌ ④ interest: 관심, '정말 하고 싶었다'와 모순
det.tip: fear(두려움)와 courage(용기)의 대비. 관심과 의지는 있었지만 용기가 부족했다.

questions.passage: I was about to take the lead in the race when I suddenly felt a pain in my knee. I fell to the ground and had to be carried off the track. ① At first, I didn't think much of the injury. ② I thought I would get better soon. ③ Regular exercise can help improve your overall health and fitness. ④ But the test results from the hospital were not hopeful.
questions.stem: 글의 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

det.korean: ③은 규칙적 운동과 건강에 대한 일반론으로, 부상 경과 이야기와 무관하다.

❌ ①: 부상을 대수롭지 않게 여김 — 맥락 적절
❌ ②: 곧 나을 것이라 생각 — 맥락 적절
❌ ④: 검사 결과 희망적이지 않음 — 맥락 적절
det.tip: 주제 흐름: 부상→대수롭지 않게 여김→회복 기대→결과 불길. ③만 주제 이탈.

I delivered my speech to the entire school.
questions.stem: 글의 흐름과 관계없는 문장은?

det.korean: ③은 의사소통 기술과 직업 분야에 대한 일반론으로, 연설대회 결심 이야기와 무관하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③: 포스터→결심→참가 흐름에서 직업적 의사소통은 이탈
❌ ①: 내면의 목소리 — 결심 과정 적절
❌ ②: 등록 결심 — 맥락 적절
❌ ④: 결과 보고 — 맥락 적절
det.tip: 주제 흐름: 포스터 발견→내면 목소리→등록→실행. ③만 직업/전문 분야 이야기로 이탈.

questions.passage: Today, thanks to my brave decision, I am studying to be a star on the sidelines instead of on the playing field. But my act of courage taught me a valuable lesson: I can do anything that I put my mind to.
questions.stem: Olivia와 Yuna의 이야기에서 공통적으로 발견되는 교훈은?
ch: 다른 사람의 도움 없이는 어려움을 극복할 수 없다.
두려움을 직면하고 결단을 내리면 새로운 길이 열린다.
어린 시절의 꿈을 끝까지 포기하지 않아야 한다.

✅ ② 두 사람 모두 두려움/문제를 직면하고 용감한 결단을 내림
❌ ① 두 사람 모두 스스로 결단함, 타인 도움이 핵심이 아님
❌ ③ 실패가 아닌 두려움 극복이 핵심
❌ ④ Olivia는 원래 꿈(선수)을 포기하고 새 길을 찾았음
det.tip: 공통 키워드: brave decision, act of courage. 두려움 직면 + 결단 = 새로운 가능성.

det.korean: 다행히 점원이 의식(consciousness)을 되찾았다.
det.analysis:

❌ awareness: 유사하지만 원문 불일치
det.tip: regain consciousness = 의식을 되찾다. consciousness(의식) — 명사형.

This / fear / kept / me / behind / the stage / rather than / on it
